Actually description: DIBAL-H reduces esters and nitriles to aldehydes. Reaction: carbon-oxygen bond broken, another carbon-oxygen bond order changes from 2 to 1, forming aliphatic hydroxyl functional group. So forward reaction: ester -> aldehyde + aliphatic hydroxyl? Wait DIBAL-H reduces ester to aldehyde, not forming hydroxyl. But maybe they consider the reduction of ester to aldehyde, breaking C-O bond (the O-alkyl) and reducing C=O to C-OH (aldehyde has C=O still). Actually aldehyde still has C=O double bond, not hydroxyl. Hmm maybe they refer to reduction of ester to alcohol? DIBAL-H can reduce ester to aldehyde, but also can reduce nitrile to aldehyde. The description says "forming a 'aliphatic hydroxyls' functional group". That suggests product has an aliphatic hydroxyl (alcohol). Maybe they consider the reduction of ester to primary alcohol? But DIBAL-H typically stops at aldehyde unless excess. Could be ambiguous.
